status: In text.json (Fable, 2026-11-09), for Sky's read on briefs/102/fable/guard-call.html before Latch builds them in. The rows carry `hand` (no run of the style loop replaces them); not scored (a judge run needs Sky's approval). Each line was read in every case `cases` lists, and each row before and after the other speaker's lines.
why: Brief 102, Sky's calls on the guard (2026-11-09): option 1, the turned guard leaves his door when called, and step 4, nobody acts on a call after the cell's violence. Engine 0.51.0 (Keel, briefs/102/keel/report-turned-guard-call.md); Motive's spec, briefs/102/motive/turned-guard.md §1.3, §1.4, §2.2.
keys: A row or scene `about` the guard is his own call (the one called is the one who leaves: HostCall.SummonAbout, Game.LureCalled); rows without `about` stay Inez's call's. The he-warns scene is keyed by `outcome`, since who warns on a pressed visit is not who called.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: Fine. My break starts now.
All right. The door can do without me.
rows.cases: Paid, helped or pressured (a Mercenary takes all three): business-like or grudging, never thanks for money that may not have been paid.
rows.where: His yes to the Fixer at his door; he is on his feet there whenever a call works.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: Against my better judgement. All right.
For you, then. I'll step away.
rows.cases: A Loyal guard is turned only by Help (people.rules: his Pay and Pressure replies are suspicious), so he owes the Fixer a kindness and bends his duty.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: You? In the middle of your shift?
Well, this is a surprise.
rows.cases: She never sent for him (his own call) and may know nothing of the cell: surprise, warm.
rows.where: At her post, where the visit meets her (brief 022).

rows.speaker: guard
lines: Thought I'd come and see you.
Just looking in on you.
rows.cases: He came on the Fixer's word and gives her his own reason.
rows.where: Unpressed only: a pressed visit plays a warning.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: Now's no good. Leave it.
That'll have to keep.
rows.cases: summon-busy from his end: Inez down (knocked out, tied or dead, and he may not know it), or he isn't free (just come round and walking back, in a fight, or away from his door on an earlier visit: walking over, with her, walking back). No reason given, so nothing is untrue when he doesn't know she's down; said to the Fixer.
rows.where: Read before and after each of Inez's two lines, and alone.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: I've been away once. I'm not pushing my luck.
Not again. I'm staying on this door.
rows.cases: He is back at his door, been away once on either call.
rows.where: busy comes first, so he is at the door.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: With the alarm up? I'm going nowhere.
Not while they're out searching.
rows.cases: Alert is checked after busy: he is at his door and on his feet.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: Too far to go on a break.
I'd never get there and back in time.
rows.cases: At his door; her post is too long a walk.

rows.speaker: guard
lines: Inez isn't out. There's no sense going over.
With her indoors? I'd only be standing about.
rows.cases: Off the street from his end is hers (his pose is null only when he is down, which is person-down on his call): she is indoors with no post. He watches her café, so he knows she isn't out; the briefing names her.
rows.where: Unreached in the Handover: Inez always has her post.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: Who was that, love?
Who's that on at you?
rows.cases: Only within earshot of him (HostCall.TieHears from his end; never when she is down): she hears his side of a call she knows nothing of.
rows.where: Beside him on a visit, or near him dazed or fighting.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: Who wants you off that door again?
You've done enough running about, love.
rows.cases: Near him at his door; she knows he has been off it once, to see her.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: Quite right. Stay where you are, love.
Good. Don't you move from there.
rows.cases: Near his door with the alarm up: she agrees he should stay.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: Who's sending you all that way?
Tell them no, love.
rows.cases: She hears him say it's too far; she doesn't know who asked.
rows.where: Within earshot only; unreached in the Handover.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: He's not answering.
No answer. That's not like him.
rows.cases: Inez's call, the guard down (knocked out, tied or dead) and she doesn't know it: she tries him and nobody answers. Untrue if she found him, saw him carried or was told: the host's pick, and Keel's read if those can happen.
rows.where: In place of her summon-busy line; he says nothing.

scenes.result: The guard took the call. He has left the door.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: It's time, officer. Take your break now.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Good man.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Officer? Now would suit us. Off you go.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Thank you, officer.

scenes.result: The guard took the call. He has left the door.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Officer, it's time. Could you step away from the door?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Thank you. I know what it costs you.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: We're ready, officer. I'm sorry to ask it of you.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: You're a good man. Thank you.

scenes.title: The guard is at the café
scenes.result: The guard is at the café, away from the door.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Look who's left his door.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Thought you could do with some company.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: On a working day? You'll set tongues wagging.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Let them wag.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Got a moment for me?

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: For you? Always. What's brought you over?

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Nothing much. I wanted to see you.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Then stay a little.

scenes.title: The guard warns Inez
scenes.result: The guard warned Inez, and is hurrying back to his door.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Somebody knows about us, Inez. I can't stop.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Knows? What do you mean, knows?

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Keep your head down. I have to go.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Someone's found out about us. I have to get back.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Found out? Who has, love?

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Not now. Mind how you go.

edits.why: The Call card on the turned guard (offered under option 1). The base line, "Call Inez to draw the guard off the door", is wrong on him. It says what the order does and names nobody he'd go to (Motive §1.3: no name of who would come or where he'd go before the tie is known).

edits.why: Under option 1 summon-busy is also "she's down" when the guard is called (GameCall.cs SummonRefusal). The old line said only the guard. Inez down never reaches this code on her own call (person-down comes first), nor the guard down on his, so "Inez or the guard is down" is always the partner. The Handover's briefing names the pair, so its base line may.
